content:
Requirement R20 (input): Command Handover. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to command a control handover of a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-20.1, F-20.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-20.<F>.1, Be-20.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-20.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Allow the pilot to issue the actual handover command that executes transfer of UAV control back to the UAV Pilot.

R19 already covered the *request* leg (initiate handover request → UAV Pilot ack). R20 is the *commit/execute* leg (UC 8.2): pilot issues handover command → connection broken → status hidden → completion confirmed. This mirrors the R09(request)/R10(commit) split for takeover.

Function candidates:

**F-20.1 — Issue the handover-execute command.**
The teleology: give the pilot the means to commit the confirmed handover, terminating own control of the UAV. Directly maps to 8.2.12–8.2.14. This is the core, distinct from R19's request.

**F-20.2 — Confirm handover completion to the pilot (control relinquished).**
Teleology: make the pilot aware the transfer actually completed and own control is gone (8.1.17–8.1.18). Distinct goal from commanding — it's post-execution awareness. Note: this is largely R08 notification territory + R12/R13 status-hide (8.1.16). Likely satisfiable by reuse rather than new Function; flagging that.

**F-20.3 — Gate the handover-execute behind confirmation state.**
Teleology: ensure execute is only offered/armed when a valid takeover/handover context and acknowledgment exists (analogous to R10's confirmation-gating). Prevents accidental relinquish of an active UAV.

My recommendation: close on **F-20.1** as primary. F-20.2 is better absorbed by R08/R12/R13 reuse (state it as shared, not a new Function). F-20.3 is a *property* of F-20.1's behaviour (confirmation-gated commit, like R10) rather than a separate goal — I'd fold it into Be.

Which do you want to keep?
same logic as before, mirror the command takeover

Mirroring R10 (Command Takeover): closed on a single Function — the confirmation-gated one-shot commit.

**F-20.1 — Command handover execution (confirmation-gated one-shot commit).**
Pilot issues the handover-execute command; offered only once the R19 request is acknowledged. Completion awareness (8.1.17–8.1.18) and status-hide (8.1.16) are handled by reuse of R08 notifications + R12/R13 status panel — not new Functions.

**F-20.1 closed.**

Moving to Behaviour.

Mirroring Be-10 (three ack-enabled surfaces, one-shot commit), per-modality:

**Be-20.1.1 — Touch:** single tap on an armed HANDOVER commit affordance (enabled only after R19 ack). Confirmation-gated: the control is inert/greyed until the acknowledged state arms it; one tap commits, breaks connection, triggers completion notification.

**Be-20.1.2 — Keyboard:** bezel OSS / UCP discrete press on the same armed HANDOVER action; one-shot commit, same gating.

**Be-20.1.3 — Mixed:** not additive here — commit is a single atomic action, no compound sub-steps to split. Same as R10, I'd skip a distinct mixed pathway; redundancy is Touch-OR-Keyboard on the shared armed control.

Both paths modality-complete (either alone completes the commit). Recommend closing on **Be-20.1.1 + Be-20.1.2** as the redundant pair.

Agree?
same logic as before, mirror the initiate takeover

Correction noted — mirror R10 (Command/commit takeover), which is what R20 corresponds to (8.2 execute leg). R10 closed on a confirmation-gated one-shot commit offered via **three shared surfaces**: dedicated button, option-ring segment, UAV detail-panel row.

**Be-20.1.1 — Touch:** one-shot HANDOVER commit affordance, armed only after R19 ack, surfaced on all three shared surfaces (dedicated button, option-ring segment, detail-panel row). Single tap commits.

**Be-20.1.2 — Keyboard:** same armed HANDOVER commit via bezel OSS / UCP discrete press.

Both modality-complete, confirmation-gated, one-shot. No distinct Mixed pathway (atomic action).

**Be-20.1.1 + Be-20.1.2 closed.**

Structure — mirroring R10/R19 (which already bound a HANDOVER action to the same three structures):

**S-20.1.1.1 — Reused three-surface commit set with HANDOVER-EXECUTE binding.**
- Dedicated command button (WAD, shared R09/R10/R19) — adds armed HANDOVER-EXECUTE state.
- Option-ring segment (shared press-hold ring, R05/R14/R17/R19) — HANDOVER-EXECUTE segment.
- UAV detail-panel row (shared R12/R13/R16 chassis) — HANDOVER-EXECUTE row.
- Bezel OSS + UCP (Keyboard) mapped to the same armed action.
- Arming driven by R19-ack state; completion + status-hide via reused R08 notification stack + R12/R13 panel (8.1.16–8.1.18).

This is pure reuse — R19 already added the HANDOVER binding to these surfaces; R20 adds only the *execute/commit* state (armed-after-ack) alongside R19's *request* state, exactly as R10 sat atop R09.

No second structure candidate needed — the three-surface pattern is the established convention. Close R20?

**R20 closed.**

- **F-20.1** — Command handover execution (confirmation-gated one-shot commit); mirrors R10. Completion awareness and status-hide absorbed by R08/R12/R13 reuse, not new Functions.
- **Be-20.1.1** (Touch) + **Be-20.1.2** (Keyboard) — one-shot HANDOVER-EXECUTE commit, armed only after R19 ack, surfaced on the three shared surfaces; modality-complete, no distinct Mixed pathway.
- **S-20.1.1.1** — reused three-surface commit set (dedicated button, option-ring segment, detail-panel row) + bezel OSS/UCP, adding only the armed HANDOVER-EXECUTE state atop R19's request binding; arming from R19-ack state; completion/status-hide via R08 + R12/R13.

Pure reuse — R20 sits atop R19 exactly as R10 sat atop R09.
